mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing near-term S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during pre-tightening periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and equity valuations, pushing 20-day S&P 500 returns positively.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS up > 10,000 and UNRATE down > 0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day returns show no significant correlation with the labor strength signal (Pearson IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in personal consumption expenditures (indirect proxy via GDPC1 quarterly growth) ahead of the decision date creates excess demand, pushing up equity valuations and generating positive 60-day forward S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 4% in the preceding quarter
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative despite the demand signal (t-test p < 0.01).

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in consumer goods orders (not available in the catalog) would typically signal supply-side weakness, but here we proxy with RSAFS (retail sales) falling while HOUST (housing starts) rises, suggesting mixed but cautiously supportive supply conditions that fail to strongly impact 5-day forward returns.
When the monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2% for two consecutive months, the market anticipates a protracted tightening cycle, causing a sharp decline in 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not lower than during low-inflation periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% for three months, without a corresponding rise in jobless claims (not available), suggests labor market resilience that boosts investor sentiment and drives positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns show no statistically significant correlation with UNRATE trend (Pearson IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (proxy via PAYEMS) exceeding 130,000 and a simultaneous 3-month upward trend in housing starts (HOUST) indicate expanding demand in both consumption and investment sectors, which tends to lift equity valuations and produce positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 130,000 for 3 months and HOUST rising trend
failure_condition: 20-day returns are flat or negative despite the combined demand and housing signals (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), a sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 90 signals supply-side stress that dampens equity risk premia, resulting in negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and INDPRO < 90 in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not statistically lower than during non-tightening periods (Rank IC > -0.1).
